name: Typecho
description: Typecho is a lightweight, open-source PHP blogging platform with a Markdown editor, pages, categories and tags, threaded comments, themes, plugins and an XML-RPC API for desktop and mobile editors. This script installs the official release with nginx, PHP-FPM and SQLite and completes the setup with upstream's command-line installer, so no setup page is ever left open.

app_vars.name: var_admin_pass
app_vars.label: Admin Password
app_vars.help: Generated when empty. Shown at the end of the install output either way.

notes.text: The admin password is generated during install and shown at the end of the install output, together with the username. Log in at http://<IP>/admin/ and replace the placeholder email address admin@localhost.local in your profile.
The site address is set to http://<container IP>, and Typecho builds every link from it. Change it under Settings > Basic when the IP changes or the blog sits behind a reverse proxy or domain.

Everything that is not core code lives in /opt/typecho_data: config.inc.php, the SQLite database typecho.db, and usr/ with themes, plugins and uploads. /opt/typecho/usr and /opt/typecho/config.inc.php are links into it. Back up /opt/typecho_data.

Updates replace only the core files, as upstream's upgrade guide does, and leave usr/ alone: the bundled themes are not refreshed, and edits made with the theme editor survive. After an update, open /admin/ and confirm the database upgrade Typecho asks for.

The interface is set to English using the language pack from typecho/languages, the timezone to UTC instead of upstream's UTC+8, and pretty URLs without index.php are on. All three can be changed in the settings.
